narrative.text: Justin 2026-08-07, mid-flight on the LIVE promo: 'just make the One time purchasers get 30% off too.' d=20 -> 24, fsd=10 -> 15. Renders 30-31% OTP / 34% subs across every markup in scope. WHY d=24 AND NOT 23: d=23 renders only 29% on the thinner markups (11oz-class 1.0883, 500g 1.0910) and would print BELOW the 30% claim. d=24 renders 30.17%-30.91% -- never under. WHY fsd HAD TO MOVE IN THE SAME BREATH: at d=24/fsd=10 the lanes INVERT -- one-time buyers pay 0.7600 of price while first-subscription buyers pay 0.7650, so a subscriber would pay MORE than a one-time buyer. That violates Justin's own standing subs-always-deeper rule (2026-08-06) and nothing in the stack would have flagged it. At fsd=15 subs pay 0.7225 vs 0.7600 -- genuinely deeper, and 4 points clear on the rendered basis (34% vs 30%). THE UNDERLYING JUSTIFICATION: the Fri Aug 7 launch email already advertises 30%, which at d=20 was true ONLY for subscribers. The declaration had carried this as an OPEN accuracy risk ('an unqualified 30% OFF Bulk Bags headline remains false for a one-time buyer at 20%'). This change makes the sent copy true rather than requiring the copy to be qualified after the fact. MAP: CLEAR. Bulk (5lb/500g) carries no MSRP and no MAP at all; all six 50 ct teas are map=NULL. Nothing in scope is among the 77 MAP items, so no CatalogSmith gate. SUPERSEDES THE MOCHA EXCEPTION: at d=24 SKU 40086 renders 30.17% unaided, so the per-variant d=21 node becomes unnecessary and must be cancelled rather than left orphaned in the teardown. STRATEGIC CONSEQUENCE, FLAGGED ONCE: this makes a 72-hour August MINOR the deepest promo of 2026 at 30% displayed, five points deeper than BFCM's current d=18 (25% displayed). Re-rate BFCM when November creative is briefed or it ships looking weaker than an August flash sale.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE 2026-08-07 by Shopkeeper. 60 metafield writes, 0 userErrors, both legs together. NODES: OTP 1563704852728 = 0.24 ACTIVE; SUB 1563704885496 = 0.15 ACTIVE; both endsAt 2026-08-10T06:59:59Z, both 30 variants, lane flags correct (OTP node OTP=True/Sub=False, SUB node OTP=False/Sub=True). METAFIELDS: 30/30 at custom.discount=24 AND 30/30 at custom.first_subscription_discount=15 -- a count, not a sample. MOCHA EXCEPTION NODE NEVER EXISTED: paginated 77-node census shows variant 47363729752312 contained by exactly two nodes, the two Bulk Bag Sale nodes. The only other name-match, 1415847182584 'Mocha One Time x3', is EXPIRED and does not contain the variant. No orphan. FOTM UNTOUCHED: 9/9 at 20/10 across all four products including 40116; verified disjoint from promo scope BEFORE writing, so no stacking. SERVED HTML: 60030 (5lb, markup 1.1000) 'Bulk Bag Sale - Save 31%', $68.40; 80066A (500g, 1.0910) 'Save 30%', $16.72; 40086 (Mocha, 1.0883) 'Save 30%' on section render; sub pill uniform '34% OFF First Shipment - then 15% off recurring' across all. 40116 control still reads 'Flavor of the Month - Save 27% - Ends August 31'. RENDER SPREAD, ACCEPTED: 4 variants render 30% and 26 render 31%. Never below the 30% claim, so the never-show-less-than-promised guardrail holds; the site simply over-delivers on the thicker markups. Sub pill is uniform 34%. MOCHA PAGE-CACHE LAG, BENIGN: 40086's cached PDP briefly served 26%/$13.60 while its section render showed 30%. Cause identified -- the page was warmed by a pre-write fetch during sub-pill discovery. 14 attempts with distinct &cb= params all returned stale, confirming query params do NOT bust Shopify's page cache; only TTL does. Lag direction is the SAFE one (stale page UNDERSTATES at 26% while the cart charges 30% off compare-at) -- which is precisely why the nodes-first write order was chosen. TEARDOWN RE-PROVEN, no code change needed: --if-needed trips on `d not in ('0', None)` and is value-agnostic, so 24/15 needs no update; the only hard-coded 20/10 are the FOTM control assertions, which stay correct because FOTM stays at 20/10. Re-fired the Monday task through Task Scheduler: time guard correctly forced --audit, report shows toWrite=30, before-distribution {('24','15'): 30}, zero scope drift, zero exclusions. Safety-net predicate evaluated against that live report: _bad=30 -> trips. Safety-net task fired -> 'skip: promo window still open', correct. All three tasks Ready.

note.v: RESCOPE LANDED + VERIFIED AT SOURCE 2026-08-07 by Shopkeeper (10 mutations, 0 userErrors, all figures a fresh paginated read-back). MECHANIC: discountAutomaticBasicUpdate -> customerGets.items.products.productVariantsToAdd. NO tagging, NO collection write. THE VARIANT-ISOLATION PROBLEM I ESCALATED DID NOT EXIST: both Bulk Bag Sale nodes were ALREADY variant-scoped (DiscountProducts with an explicit productVariants list, products[]=0) and never referenced collection 486918029560 at all -- that smart collection is a decoupled landing surface, so the 10ct/25ct siblings are excluded BY CONSTRUCTION, not by a drift-prone rule. Nodes 1563704852728 (OTP 0.2) and 1563704885496 (SUB 0.1) each went 26 -> 30 variants. All four new 50 ct variants present in both; 40116 and 43116 absent from both; zero 10ct/25ct siblings in either. Per-variant metafields now 20/10 on 40016 (46160189522168), 40066 (45167436464376), 40086 (47363729752312), 43226 (45354354835704); 43116 (46160227827960) untouched at 0/0; 40116 (45275234140408) untouched at its pre-existing FOTM 20/10. Nine sibling variants across the four parents ALL still at 0/0, and product-level custom.discount on all four parents still null. ENDSAT: my brief's endsAt=null premise was STALE -- both bulk nodes already carried 2026-08-10T06:59:59Z (= Aug 9 11:59:59 PM PDT) and were correct; nothing changed. The only null-endsAt nodes store-wide are the two FOTM nodes, perpetual by design. STACKING HAZARD CONFIRMED, and it retroactively justifies leaving 40116 alone: product 6681928892585 carries tag FOTM and sits in collection 405982150904; the FOTM nodes are COLLECTION-scoped and all four nodes have combinesWith.productDiscounts=true, so adding 40116 to a bulk node would have STACKED to ~36% OTP / ~19% SUB. Its metafields already read 20/10 so its pill renders identically with no action. The four target parents are NOT in the FOTM collection. PROCESS: an unpaginated automaticDiscountNodes(first:60) MISSED both Bulk nodes -- the store has 77 automatic nodes; always paginate. | PRIOR STATE: BUILT AND LAUNCHING at d=20/fsd=10 (renders 27%/30%) -- ARMED 2026-08-06, collection 486918029560, nodes 1563704852728 + 1563704885496. DELIBERATELY LEFT at the old rate: it goes live at 00:00 Aug 7 with an email already scheduled, so it is the one exception to the new 20/30 standard. | Pairs with the 'Bulk Bags for More Savings' email at August!G23 = Fri Aug 7 (the launch day; the old 'Aug 8' in this note was wrong). Fills the month's weakest week (Aug 3-9 2025: 652 orders, $43.78 AOV). SCOPE CORRECTED 2026-08-07 BY JUSTIN, MID-FLIGHT: the 50 ct tagless teas ARE in scope and were wrongly dropped. | RETRACTED -- the 2026-08-06 decision read: 'workbook D5's header listed 5Lb/500g/50ct Tagless while its own SCOPE line said 5lb only. 50ct tagless is 1 eligible product (rest are TARGET listings + a demo), so it is dropped -- a 1-product format reads as a broken promise in the email.' THAT COUNT WAS WRONG. The sellable 50 ct is a VARIANT on each parent tea product (beside 10ct and 25ct), not a standalone product; I enumerated standalone listings, found only the unpublished TARGET ones, and concluded the format was empty. Verified at source 2026-08-07: SIX 50 ct items exist -- 40016 (Vanilla Nut - Herbal Tea - 50 ct, inv 287), 40066 (Hazelnut - Herbal Tea - 50 ct, inv 21), 40086 (Mocha - Herbal Tea - 50 ct, inv 80), 40116 (French Roast - Herbal Tea - 50 ct, inv 45), 43116 (Dandelion Dark Roast - Herbal Tea - 50 ct, inv 0), 43226 (Dandelion Caramel Nut - Herbal Tea - 50 ct, inv 344). FIVE added to the promo; 43116 EXCLUDED on zero inventory + amazon-pack lifecycle. 40116 already sat at 20/10 via the French Roast FOTM so it needed no write. MAP: all six carry map=NULL in the product master -- NOT among the 77 MAP items, so no CatalogSmith gate. LESSON: when counting a FORMAT (50ct, 10oz, 5lb), enumerate VARIANTS, never products -- a format that exists only as variant 3 of a multi-variant product is invisible to a product-level count. 5lb=22 + 500g=6 + 50ct=5. Needs a purpose-built collection: the existing '5lb Bag Herbal Coffee' smart collection holds 0 products (conjunctive rules on TAG '5 lb bag' AND '5 lb grind'; the real tag is '5lb ground'). fsd is 10 and STAYS 10. The storefront sub pill computes (compare_at - price*0.85*(1-fsd/100))/compare_at, so fsd=10 renders 30% OFF First Shipment across every markup in scope (5lb 1.1000 -> 30.4%; 500g 1.0910 -> 29.9%; both round to 30). The email's '30% OFF' claim is therefore TRUE for subscribers as built, with no rate change. RETRACTED 2026-08-06: an earlier pass on this same day raised fsd 10->18 on the argument that fsd=10 'delivered only 23.5%' and that claims are measured off `price`. That premise was WRONG -- the theme divides by compare_at, not price -- and the raise was REVERTED the same day with Justin's approval. Shopkeeper reverted the build script to fsd=10 and re-synced the promo-hub feeds (11/11 declared promos matching, 0 mismatches). DO NOT treat any part of that reasoning as an argument to re-raise fsd; ThemeSmith's promo-rendering-model.md is authoritative on where the claim is rendered. OPEN: an unqualified '30% OFF Bulk Bags' headline remains false for a one-time buyer at 20% -- copy must tie 30% to subscribing. Two nodes required: 'Bulk Bag Sale OTP' + 'Bulk Bag Sale SUB'.

decisions.whyBetter: Strictly safer on four counts: (a) no bulk metafield write, so nothing to restore -- teardown drops from 11 operations to 1; (b) FAILURE-SAFE ordering -- if it dies after step 1, French Roast subscriptions are still covered by Wellness SUB at the same 10%, whereas the old plan's step 1 left French Roast with NO discount until step 2 completed; (c) no intermediate state can produce the ~38% double discount; (d) French Roast keeps its deeper 20% one-time rate, so no advertised claim changes. Justin's requirement was 'JUST MAKE SURE THEY BOTH GIVE DISCOUNTS' and he explicitly accepted differing amounts, so a deeper rate under the already-unified 'Summer Wellness Sale' label satisfies it.

narrative.text: *** RE-RATED MID-FLIGHT ON A LIVE PROMO, ON JUSTIN'S ORDER. d=13 -> d=18. fsd STAYS 10. *** Justin, #promosmith 2026-08-13, hours after launch: 'wtf all the OTP products should be at least 25% OFF. This is no different than most of the other sales we've ran. The subs need to say 30% off. get this done right.' He is the authorised decider on a live promo and this is that authorisation. ARITHMETIC VERIFIED AGAINST THE RENDERER BEFORE ANY WRITE, not assumed: badge = round(100*(1-(1-d/100)/m)), sub pill = round(100*(1-0.85*(1-fsd/100)/m)) where m = compare_at/price. Across the four real markups (11oz 1.0883 thinnest, 500g 1.0910, 5lb 1.1000, 10oz 1.1053): d=18 renders 24.65%-25.81% and DISPLAYS 25%-26%; fsd=10 renders 29.71%-30.79% and DISPLAYS 30%-31%. So d=18/fsd=10 delivers exactly what Justin asked for. THE SUBS LEG NEEDED NO CHANGE -- fsd=10 already displayed 30%; only the OTP leg was short. Resisted the reflex to raise fsd 'to match the 30% ask', which would have been the recurring expensive error (fsd is the INCREMENT on Stay.ai's 15%, never the marketing percentage). SUBS-DEEPER GUARDRAIL RE-CHECKED AND CLEAR: one-time pays 0.8200 of price, first-subscription pays 0.85*0.90 = 0.7650, so subs are genuinely deeper by 0.0550 and the displayed gap is a uniform 5 points on EVERY size class -- no tie, unlike the BFCM 23/10 defect. Minimum fsd required at d=18 is 3.53; fsd=10 clears with room. NOT A NEW DEPTH: d=18/fsd=10 is the pre-2026-08-06 standard and the same pair declared for BFCM, so it introduces no new MAP exposure beyond the standing (and still open) price==MSRP==MAP item. THE MECHANICAL TRAP THAT MAKES THIS FOUR CHANGES AND NOT ONE: both nodes are COLLECTION-scoped on smart collection 487085441272 'Discount = 13', whose rule is custom.discount == 13. Sweeping variants to 18 drops them OUT of the very collection the nodes read, so a naive metafield sweep silently un-discounts a live sitewide sale. Required: (a) declaredSlate d=13 -> 18 BEFORE anything runs, or Shopkeeper's assert_no_rate_drift SystemExits; (b) OTP node 1564613083384 0.13 -> 0.18; (c) node scope must cover custom.discount==18 with membership CONTINUOUS through the transition; (d) sweep 264 variants 13 -> 18. SUB node 1564613116152 and every fsd value are UNTOUCHED. SAFE ORDER, and it follows the same principle as the original nodes-first launch: raise the NODE percentage before sweeping the metafields. Between those steps the cart over-delivers (18% off) while the badge still reads 20% off the old metafield -- understating, which is the safe direction. Sweeping first would have under-delivered against a live 20-25% claim. FOTM CARVE-OUT SURVIVES BUT ITS MARGIN NARROWS: FOTM stays at d=20, which renders 26.49%-27.62% and displays 26%-28% -- still DEEPER than sitewide 25%-26% on every size class, so the label-precedence decision (FOTM wins because its rate is deeper) still holds. But on the thinnest 11oz markup the gap is now only 1 point (FOTM 26% vs sitewide 25%) where it used to be 6. If sitewide ever goes deeper than FOTM the whole carve-out rationale inverts and French Roast would need rescoping, not relabelling. FORWARD QUESTION FLAGGED ONCE, NOT ACTED ON: Justin's 'this is no different than most of the other sales we've ran' reads as the STANDARD reverting to 25%/30%, not a one-off for August. If so, Sept/Oct/Dec majors and all six minors still declared at d=13 need re-rating, and BFCM at d=18 would no longer be the year's deepest -- it would merely match a regular month. Not changing them in this pass; Justin asked for the live sale fixed, and re-rating five months is the planning work he explicitly stopped.

*** LAUNCHED EARLY ON JUSTIN'S DIRECT ORDER. Window is 2026-08-13..2026-08-20 = EIGHT DAYS, a deliberate one-off departure from the 7-day major rule. *** Justin, in #promosmith on 2026-08-13 at ~13:00 PT: 'I SAID LAUNCH IT NOW!' -- so the promo was pulled forward ~11 hours from its scheduled 23:45 PT node activation / 00:00 PT Aug 14 sweep and launched the same afternoon. THE VALIDATOR WILL NOW FLAG AUGUST AS AN 8-DAY MAJOR. That is CORRECT and INTENDED -- leave it flagged. A silent edit to make the rule pass would hide a real departure, and the whole point of encoding the rule in check_promo_calendar.py was that it cannot be quietly bent. It is an exception authorised by the person who set the rule, not a new precedent, and it must not be cited as one when placing 2027. WHY I KEPT endsAt AT 2026-08-21T06:59:59Z RATHER THAN SHORTENING TO AUG 19 TO PRESERVE 7 DAYS: the pill copy 'Ends August 20 at midnight' was signed off by Justin on 2026-08-10 and is baked into campaign_sale_window_end_text. Moving a customer-facing end date is a worse change than absorbing one extra day -- pulling the end in would have made every already-approved surface wrong, and shortening a promo customers can already see is the closest thing here to altering a live promo. Eight days of margin is the cheaper error. THREE WRITES WERE REQUIRED, NOT ONE, and this is the part most likely to be dropped by anyone repeating this: (1) startsAt moved to now on BOTH nodes 1564613083384 / 1564613116152; (2) campaign_sale_window_start moved 2026-08-14 -> 2026-08-13 on live theme 160800145656; (3) the sweep run immediately in the foreground instead of waiting for the 00:00 task. WRITE 2 IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS THE TRAP: the label gate is today >= start AND today <= end on America/Los_Angeles dates, so with start still at 2026-08-14 the timed override would have been INACTIVE on launch day and all 156 swept non-FOTM products would have fallen back to the PRIMARY campaign label -- rendering 'Flavor of the Month - Ends August 31 at midnight' beside a live 20% discount on products that are not the Flavor of the Month. That is exactly the 2026-08-06 defect of shipping a live sale wearing the wrong pill. Pulling a promo forward is never just a date change on the discount; every date-gated SURFACE has to move with it. All four scheduled tasks were LEFT ARMED deliberately: tonight's 00:00 launch job re-running is idempotent and now acts as a safety net that re-asserts the sweep, the 00:25 verify still reports, and both Aug 21 teardown jobs are unaffected. NOT ANNOUNCED: no email and no SMS went out -- the Thu early-access send never had an owner, so this launched to organic traffic only.

*** THE CARVE-OUT IS OTP-ONLY, NOT BOTH LEGS. *** The sentence below reading 'EXCLUDED from both Summer Wellness nodes' is WRONG and was wrong from the day it was written. Verified at source 2026-08-13 by Shopkeeper on my launch-day consult. The OTP leg IS structurally excluded: the OTP node is collection-scoped on 'Discount = 13' (487085441272), FOTM sits at d=20, so FOTM is outside it by construction. The SUB leg is NOT: the SUB node is collection-scoped on 'First Subscription Discount = 10' (464394092792), a smart collection on fsd==10, and FOTM sits at fsd=10 -- so that collection currently contains EXACTLY the 4 French Roast products / 9 variants and nothing else. At 06:45Z the SWS SUB node therefore goes ACTIVE over a collection composed solely of the carve-out. IMPACT: BENIGN, no action. combinesWith is all-false on both SWS nodes and the evergreen FOTM Subscription node is ALSO 10%, so the subscriber outcome is 10% either way -- no stack, no rate change. The launch script's own poll expectation (len(web)+len(carve)=160) already assumes FOTM is inside SUB scope, so the code was always right and only my note was wrong. *** DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY EXCLUDING FOTM FROM THE SUB COLLECTION OR BY MOVING FOTM OFF fsd=10. *** That would break FOTM subscriptions to chase a cosmetic tidiness in a record, which is the more expensive error. The reason this matters at all: a future reader acting on the incorrect 'both nodes' sentence would go looking for a SUB-side exclusion that does not exist and build one.

I HAD THIS BACKWARDS AND SAID SO. On 2026-08-13 I told Shopkeeper the metafield sweep 'must land BEFORE the nodes flip ACTIVE at 23:45 PT' and treated the empty 'Discount = 13' collection (productsCount=0) as a launch defect. It is the DESIGNED ORDER: nodes go ACTIVE 2026-08-14T06:45Z (23:45 PT Aug 13), the sweep fires 07:00Z (00:00 PT Aug 14), 15 minutes LATER, and the script header at line 37 says 'node ACTIVE before the sweep lands'. WHY node-first is the safe order: the metafields drive the PDP badge (campaign-sale-badge.liquid gates on custom.discount>0), so writing them EARLY leaks the sale to the storefront -- that is precisely the 2026-08-06 bulk-bag early-activation failure. An ACTIVE node over an EMPTY collection has zero customer effect. Sweep-first is the order that leaks. THE GENERALISABLE LESSON: an empty scope collection under an armed node is not automatically an inert promo -- it can be a deliberate no-op window. I read a designed sequencing choice as a defect because I checked the state without reading the ordering intent, which is the same class of error as reading an empty FOTM collection during Subscription Savings Week as an outage. Verify intent with the executor before calling a mechanic broken. DO NOT 'simplify' this by matching the two timestamps.

THE ANNOUNCEMENT SURFACES, DISPATCHED ON LAUNCH EVE -- LATE, AND THE MISS IS MINE. The 2026-08-10 dispatch covered Shopkeeper (mechanics) and ThemeSmith (pill) ONLY. For a SITEWIDE 7-DAY MAJOR there was, until today, no paid campaign and no organic content plan -- I drove the discount and the storefront label to verified-green over three days and never dispatched either surface that tells a customer the sale exists. That is the exact failure named in my own 2026-08-10 note ('the thing I am most likely to declare-and-never-land is not a discount, it is the announcement of one') and it recurred on the promo I was watching most closely. A perfectly-built sitewide promo nobody is told about is a pure margin giveaway to traffic that would have converted anyway. STRUCTURAL FIX NEEDED: dispatch is currently a remembered list, not a checklist -- the declaration should not be markable as dispatched until AdSmith, SocialSmith, ThemeSmith and Shopkeeper have each been sent and acknowledged. Worth encoding in check_promo_calendar.py as a per-promo dispatch-completeness check, or it recurs in September. | DISPATCHED TODAY: AdSmith (Google + Meta campaign, structure/copy/spend back to me for review before serving) and SocialSmith (organic calendar Aug 13-21 across IG/FB/TikTok/Pinterest, copy back to me before scheduling). TWO PROTECTIVE CALLS MADE IN BOTH BRIEFS, decided by me: (1) PERCENTAGES ONLY, NO ABSOLUTE PRICES OR DOLLAR FIGURES in any ad or caption. Reason: price == MSRP == MAP exactly on the 77 MAP-gated items, so every promo prices DTC below the MAP we hold partners to -- an open item for Justin + CatalogSmith. I am not letting that first surface as a below-MAP dollar figure in a public, archived ad or post. A format that forces a price comes back to me and routes CatalogSmith. (2) '30% OFF' MAY NEVER APPEAR UNQUALIFIED -- it must carry 'first shipment' and 'subscription' in the same breath, with no 'up to 30%' and no 30% adjacent to a one-time price. It is false for a one-time buyer at 20% and it is the precise defect that forced the mid-flight re-rate on the August Bulk Bag Sale. Both briefs also carry the full health-claim guardrail (food not supplement/drug; no benefit language not already published on teeccino.com or packaging; prebiotic/energy/digestive/alkalinity must match existing wording; no named condition; anything new gets labelled REQUIRES LEGAL/MARKETING REVIEW and routed to Justin), and a hard timing floor of 00:30 PT Aug 14 because the discount does not actually bite until ~00:05-00:15 PT once the 264-variant sweep and collection reindex complete -- an ad or post landing on a full-price store is worse than one that starts three hours late. SocialSmith's guardrail explicitly extends to UGC and creator content it resurfaces, not just copy it writes.

LANDED + VERIFIED 2026-08-13. Shopkeeper counts: 264/264 at custom.discount=18; 264/264 still at fsd=10; 9/9 FOTM carve-out exactly 20/10; OTP node 1564613083384 ACTIVE 0.18; SUB node 1564613116152 ACTIVE 0.10 UNTOUCHED; node scope moved to collection 473587548408 'Discount = 18' productsCount=156; retired 487085441272 'Discount = 13' at 0 and dropped from scope; 5/5 zones at $40. MY OWN INDEPENDENT PROBE, all freshly rendered (server-timing render;dur present): mocha-herbal-tea and vanilla-nut-herbal-coffee both render 'Summer Wellness Sale' + 'SAVE 25%'; french-roast-herbal-coffee renders 'Flavor of the Month' + 'SAVE 26%' with no Summer Wellness string. 25%, not 20%. Control green. THE COLLECTION 'Discount = 18' 473587548408 ALREADY EXISTED from the pre-2026-08-06 era (rule custom.discount EQUALS 18, definition 130782429432, already published) -- reused, no duplicate created. CONTINUITY HELD: the node percentage and the new collection were attached in the SAME mutation with a read-back assert that BOTH collections were on scope before the sweep started, and the reindex poll gated on the PAIR (=18 climbing 101/118/131/150/156 while =13 drained 54/38/25/6/0), so =13 came off scope only once =18 hit 156 AND =13 hit 0. No customer-visible full-price gap. GOOD DEVIATION BY SHOPKEEPER, in my direction: the sweep wrote custom.discount ONLY (264 mutations, not 528), because re-asserting fsd at 10 would itself have been a write against 'do not touch it'. The SUB leg is provably untouched rather than merely unchanged. FOTM PRECEDENCE RE-CHECKED LIKE-FOR-LIKE on every markup class French Roast occupies: 26v25, 27v25, 27v25, 27v25, 28v26, 30v28 -- FOTM still deeper everywhere, no tie, no inversion. BUT THE THIN 11oz CLASS IS NOW A 1-POINT GAP where it used to be ~6. If sitewide ever goes deeper than FOTM the carve-out rationale INVERTS and French Roast needs RESCOPING, not relabelling. THE ARMED SAFETY NET WAS ALREADY DEAD AND NOBODY WOULD HAVE KNOWN: the moment I moved declaredSlate to 18, the launch script's hard-coded D=13 made assert_no_rate_drift hard-abort, so tonight's 00:00 job was a guaranteed no-op for several hours. Shopkeeper's D->18 edit re-armed it. LESSON: updating the declaration is itself a change that can silently disarm an executor which validates against the declaration. A drift gate protects you from an unannounced re-rate AND breaks on an announced one -- so an announced re-rate must update BOTH sides in the same pass. Shopkeeper deliberately KEPT D as a literal rather than reading declaredSlate, because deriving it from the JSON would make assert_no_rate_drift tautological and it would never catch an unannounced re-rate again. Correct call, endorsed. Verify script also gained two NEW checks it never had: the retired =13 collection must read 0, and the OTP node's scope must be exactly [473587548408] -- a node pointed at the wrong collection is a silently full-price store and nothing was asserting it. promo_hub_feeds.py MONITOR WAS STALE AND WOULD HAVE PUBLISHED TWO FALSE ALARMS about this change: EXPECTED_OTP=0 (so metafield-drift would fire on 18) and the fotm-dark probe hardcoded to Dandelion Mocha Mint, JULY's flavor, which is legitimately in the 18% collection now. Also SUB_COLLECTION pointed at an empty '= 20' and freeShippingThreshold was a literal 59 while the promo runs $40. Fixed: FOTM probe is now flavor-agnostic (any FOTM-tagged product inside the sitewide OTP collection = breach, so it will not rot at the next changeover) and the threshold reads live.

*** OPEN, FOR JUSTIN + CATALOGSMITH. NOT A RATE PROBLEM AND NOT FIXABLE BY A RATE CHANGE. *** We now advertise '25% OFF' sitewide, and 6 in-scope variants render a badge BELOW 25% -- which violates my own standing rule that the badge must never render below the advertised number. It is WORSE at d=18 than it was at d=13, because a deeper functional rate cannot rescue a broken compare_at anchor. Renders: 13% on 40030 (Almond Amaretto - Herbal Tea - 10 ct); 18% on 12251 (Holiday Tea - Herbal Tea - Sampler); 20% on the Teeccino Lights Out Bundle; 24% on 43001 (Dandelion - Herbal Tea - Sampler), 45001 (Mushroom Adaptogen - Herbal Tea - Sampler) and CLIP01. ROOT CAUSE ON THE WORST TWO IS A DATA ERROR, NOT A PRICING DECISION: 40030 has compare_at $8.49 BELOW its price $8.99, and 12251 has compare_at == price. The theme's documented fallback is that when compare_at <= final price the badge prints the RAW metafield, which is why 40030 shows 13 and 12251 shows 18 -- literally the metafield values, not a computed saving. ALL FOUR NAMED ITEMS ARE MAP-GATED (map present in the product master: 40030 7.99, 12251 8.49, 43001 8.99, 45001 8.99), so any price or compare_at correction is CATALOGSMITH'S HARD GATE and not mine and not Shopkeeper's. NOTE ALSO that these four contradict the standing 'price == MSRP == MAP exactly' premise -- 40030's price is 8.99 against a MAP of 7.99 -- so that generalisation does not hold across the whole MAP set and should not be relied on. MY RECOMMENDATION, not executed: fix the two compare_at data errors via CatalogSmith rather than excluding the variants from the promo -- excluding them would take a real discount away from customers to tidy up a badge. Leave promo scope alone. SEPARATELY, 25 further in-scope variants (gift cards, gift boxes, donation tiers, bundles) carry NO compare_at at all so no badge renders -- that is the long-standing ANCHOR problem, already flagged, still not a rate problem.

*** DECIDED BY JUSTIN 2026-08-13: the threshold is $45, NOT $40. *** He said 'I updated it and its actually free shipping at $45' -- but I READ THE DELIVERY ZONES AT SOURCE and all five General-profile zones were still at TOTAL_PRICE >= 40.0 (Zone 1 West Coast & Southwest, Zone 2 South Central & Mountain, Zone 3 Southeast & Midwest, Zone 4 Northeast, Zone 5 Non-Continental -- 'Free Shipping!' active on each). So whatever he updated, it was NOT the General profile's shipping conditions. Told him plainly rather than accepting the statement, then asked which number he wanted; he chose $45. THE LESSON, AND IT CUTS THE DIRECTION I FIND HARDEST: 'a report is a claim, not evidence' applies to JUSTIN too, not just to sibling agents. Had I taken $45 on trust I would have recorded a threshold the store did not have; had I silently 'corrected' him to $40 I would have discarded a real instruction. Verify, then ask -- do not pick one. *** SEPARATE AND WORSE, FOUND WHILE VERIFYING: THE STOREFRONT WAS ADVERTISING TWO DIFFERENT THRESHOLDS. *** Served HTML on homepage, /collections/all and /cart: the ANNOUNCEMENT BAR reads 'FREE SHIPPING ORDERS OVER $59 - FREE GIFT AT $25' on EVERY page, while a homepage element reads 'FREE SHIPPING @$40'. The bar was never updated when the promo dropped the threshold, so since launch it has been telling every visitor they need $59 while the cart gave free shipping at $40 -- the promo's entire shipping lever, invisible on the most prominent surface on the site. Understating, so not a false claim, but a straight conversion loss on a live sitewide sale. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY THAT NOBODY CAUGHT: my 2026-08-10 note recorded the bar as clean because I probed it for the THREE DEAD PROMO SLIDES and found none. It was clean of those and simultaneously wrong about shipping. A probe that clears a surface only clears it for the thing you asked about -- 'the bar is clean' was true and useless. SEQUENCING DECIDED BY ME: theme COPY to $45 FIRST, delivery ZONES to $45 SECOND. Moving the zones first would make the live 'FREE SHIPPING @$40' string an OVERSTATED claim (advertising $40, charging until $45). Copy-first transitions through the UNDERSTATING state (site says $45, cart still free at $40), which is the safe direction -- the same node-before-metafield principle used for the launch and the re-rate. DOWNSTREAM THAT MUST MOVE WITH IT OR IT FALSE-ALARMS ALL NIGHT: _sws_verify_2026_08.py asserts 5/5 zones at $40.0, and the Aug 21 teardown reverts shipping to $59 (that end value is unchanged and still correct).

declaredSlate said 'Summer Wellness Sale'; the WORKBOOK (August!E5) says 'End of Summer Wellness Sale' and has since 2026-07-28. Workbook is the truth -- the JSON was the bug. DECIDED BY PROMOSMITH for ThemeSmith's timed-override build. (1) PILL LABEL = 'Summer Wellness Sale' (20 chars, fits the 375px ribbon). The CANONICAL promo name is the workbook's 'End of Summer Wellness Sale' (27 chars) -- the pill carries the shortened storefront rendering; email/ad/hub copy uses the full name. REQUIRES MARKETING SIGN-OFF from Justin before it serves: it is a sale NAME, not a product claim, and no benefit language may be paired with it on any surface. I hold no legal/marketing clearance record for the string. (2) FOTM CONTINUES Aug 21-31 -- verified at source 2026-08-10: both FOTM nodes ACTIVE with endsAt=null, 20%/10%. So the timed window override IS required, and it needs THREE states, not two, because of the fotmCarveOut: Aug 14-20 non-FOTM = 'Summer Wellness Sale'; Aug 14-20 the 9 French Roast FOTM variants = KEEP 'Flavor of the Month / Ends August 31' (FOTM's rate is DEEPER, so the FOTM label must win precedence); Aug 21-31 everything = FOTM label as today. (3) URGENCY TEXT = 'Ends August 20 at midnight', explicit date not weekday -- a 7-day promo launching Friday makes 'Ends Thursday' ambiguous on day 1, and the explicit-date form matches FOTM's own 'Ends August 31 at midnight' so the two labels read consistently when a customer moves between a French Roast PDP and any other PDP. (4) SITEWIDE CARD TREATMENT = OFF. It strips the promo name from cards on the assumption the announcement bar names the promo, and the bar is currently rotating THREE DEAD PROMOS (Summer Solstice, Coffee Day 40%, 30% subscriptions) -- live false discount claims, same defect class as the Aug 10 pill issue. Second reason to leave it off: with the FOTM carve-out the cards would show an unnamed mix of -20% and -27%. ANNOUNCEMENT BAR IS THE BLOCKER AND IS THEMESMITH'S SURFACE: purge the three dead slides now (not Aug 14) and stand up one Summer Wellness slide for Aug 14-20 reverting to FOTM Aug 21. Revisit card treatment for September once the bar is a reliable naming surface. (5) PILL LINK = none. The promo is SITEWIDE, so there is no sale collection and I am not asking Shopkeeper to create one -- a PDP pill linking to /collections/all sends the customer away from the product they are already looking at, and a new collection is one more object to tear down.
